source_refs.note: Topic 21.3.2 with the E2 and E1 mechanisms and the E2 rate equation, printed pages 78-79.

blocks.text: β-elimination is a reaction in which a hydrogen atom attached to the β-carbon of the alkyl halide and the halogen atom on the adjacent carbon atom are removed from a halogenoalkane. This reaction occurs when a base attacks the β-bhydrogen atom of the halogenoalkane. The removal of the halogen takes place either simultaneously or after the removal of the hydrogen atom. Thus, an alkene molecule is obtained instead of a substitution product. These reactions take place simultaneously with substitution reactions and often compete with them. Like nucleophilic substitution, the elimination reactions can follow two types of mechanism; E2 or E1.

In E2 mechanism, the base attacks the β hydrogen atom and the leaving group leaves at the same time with the formation of a carbon-carbon double bond. The single step E2 elimination mechanism is given below.

blocks.alt: Base- with a curly arrow to a beta H of bromoethane, a curly arrow from that C-H bond to the C-C bond, and a curly arrow from the C-Br bond to Br, giving ethene + H-Base + Br-.
blocks.caption: E2 mechanism: bromoethane (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 81).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed E2 scheme has no curly arrow from the C-Br bond to Br; it is added above.

E2 reaction is bimolecular and the rate of this reaction depends upon the concentrations of the alkyl halide and the base.s Like SN2 reactions, the molecularity of E2 reactions is also two and these reactions show second order kinetics.

In E1 mechanism, like SN1 mechanism, the first step is the slow ionization of the substrate to give a carbocation. In the second step, the base attacks the β-hydrogen atom to give an alkene as a product.

blocks.alt: Step 1: 2-bromo-2-methylpropane (delta+ C, delta- Br) with equilibrium arrows marked slow gives the 3 degree carbocation + Br-. Step 2: Base- with a curly arrow to a beta H, and a curly arrow from that C-H bond to the bond to the positive carbon, fast, gives 2-methylpropene + H-Base.
blocks.caption: E1 mechanism: 2-bromo-2-methylpropane (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 81).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Step 1 of the printed E1 scheme labels one methyl group of the carbocation 'CH2'; it is CH3, as drawn above.

E1 mechanism is a unimolecular mechanism and the rate of the reaction depends only upon the concentration of the alkyl halide molecule. Primary halogenoalkanes generally follow E2 mechanism whereas tertiary halogenoalkanes follow E1 mechanism. However, secondary halogenoalkanes can show both E2 and E1 reactions according to the choice of the solvent.
